name: Thrown and assembled form
summary: A potter throws two or more separate parts and joins them at the leather-hard stage. The joined form has a shape that no single throw can make.
how: Throw each part separately, a cylinder, a disc or a bowl.
Let the parts dry to leather-hard.
Join them with slip and press them together.
Turn and smooth the join and the foot.

origin.note: Hans Coper throws parts of a vessel on the wheel and joins them into stems, discs and spades.

adoptions.via: Hans Coper joins thrown cylinders, discs and bowls into bottles and cup forms in Lucie Rie's studio.
